title: KMS/HSM operator roles and evidence catalog for Private deployments
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: This ticket captures the PRD-level requirements, clarified scope, and a sign-off checklist for operator roles and evidence artifacts related to KMS/HSM integration for Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) customers. It consolidates role definitions, audit evidence templates, and testable acceptance criteria so Security, Product, and Engineering can sign off prior to GA of customer-managed keying features.
background: Customers deploying Redwood Private require clear operator role boundaries and a reproducible evidence catalog to satisfy auditor requests. Prior PRDs covered KMS API surface and SSO integration; this document focuses on operational roles (operators, auditors, key custodians), required artifacts (audit log exports, HSM attestation reports), and acceptance tests for end-to-end evidence generation.
requirements: Define minimal RBAC role set for Private: key_admin, key_operator, auditor_readonly, deploy_admin
Map RBAC roles to SSO groups via SAML & SCIM provisioning; document group-to-role mapping
Support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys with attestation reports
Produce an evidence catalog with templates for: KMS access logs, HSM attestation, key rotation records, separation-of-duty logs
Audit log retention and tamper-evidence: configurable retention to 7y, cryptographic integrity verification
Operational onboarding runbook for granting and revoking roles, auditing access, and performing emergency key rotation
Automated export path to customer SIEM (syslog/forwarder) and a console view for evidence retrieval
clarification_notes: SCIM provisioning is required for enterprise customers requesting automated group sync; for smaller customers we accept manual mapping during onboarding
HSM attestation must include vendor-signed report (e.g., FIPS 140-2 or 140-3 level reported) and be stored in immutable evidence store
Key escrow is optional and must be explicitly requested and documented; default is no-escrow
RBAC enforcement occurs in the Private control plane; operators in a customer VPC will have only the privileges granted by mapped roles
Separation of duties: no single role should be able to both create keys and approve key usage in production; tests will validate this
scope_decisions: IN: Role definitions, mappings to SAML groups, evidence templates, automated export to SIEM, retention policy UI
OUT: Building or certifying new HSM hardware (we will integrate vendor HSMs customers bring), key escrow implementation unless requested in a paid add-on
PHASED: Live attestation refresh (periodic re-attest) targeted for post-GA; initial GA requires at-rest attestation artifact upload only
acceptance_criteria: AC1: RBAC roles implemented in Private control plane match documented role table and enforce least-privilege in accepted test cases
AC2: SSO/SAML group mapping and SCIM provisioning flows demonstrate provisioning to at least one SAML IdP (Okta) in staging
AC3: KMS integration supports customer-managed keys with HSM-backed keys; HSM attestation report is ingestible and stored in evidence catalog
AC4: Audit logs for key operations (create, rotate, use, delete) are generated, schema validated, and exportable to customer SIEM
AC5: Evidence catalog contains templates and example artifacts for auditors and a documented retrieval procedure via Console and API
AC6: Emergency key rotation playbook executes within target RTO (<= 2 hours) in simulated drills and is logged end-to-end
AC7: Security team approves the final evidence package and signs off in the checklist below

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Misconfigured SCIM mappings grant excessive privileges - Mitigation: implement dry-run mode for SCIM sync and preflight validation
Risk: Evidence tampering or log loss - Mitigation: write-once evidence store with signed hashes and export verification
Risk: Third-party HSM vendor incompatibility - Mitigation: verify with vendor emulator early in integration and add vendor compatibility tests
Risk: Long retention costs for audit logs - Mitigation: expose retention tiers and lifecycle policies to customers and recommend compressed archival
notes_for_onboarding: During pilot onboarding (Acme Health) verify SCIM group naming matches customer directory and run the ‘role-dryrun’ to preview granted privileges. Collect HSM attestation artifact and upload to evidence catalog before completing onboarding checklist.
